summary: 미국의 농경지역중 아이오와는 계절 기온차가 심해 4계절 윤작이 불가능한 상태입니다. 우리는 NASA POWER데이터와 드론과 로버를 통한 데이터 오차감쇠를 통한 특정지역 상태 파악 후 농장물을 추천하는 방안을 제안드립니다.

Overview & How It Works Our project is a farmer-centric crop rotation decision-support framework designed for North-Central Iowa (43.15°N, -93.20°W), where extreme seasonal climate swings make continuous year-round cash-crop farming impossible. Using 20 years (2006–2025) of NASA POWER / MERRA-2 daily meteorological and soil datasets, our system analyzes Growing Degree Days (GDD), frost dates, and surface-to-root soil wetness (GWETTOP, GWETROOT) to recommend tailored seasonal crop rotations—such as pairing summer corn and nitrogen-fixing soybeans with winter-hardy cereal rye cover crops. Rather than forcing a rigid schedule, the tool provides data-backed crop recommendations and optimal planting/termination windows while leaving the final management decision to the farmer.

To overcome the coarse spatial resolution (~50 km) and seasonal bias of satellite datasets, we designed a multi-tier sensor fusion architecture combining NASA satellite data with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs). A Kalman Filter data-assimilation engine fuses daily NASA hydrological trends with periodic UAV/UGV field measurements, reducing soil moisture estimation error (RMSE) by ~51%.
